items.summary: Create, list, toggle and delete are all wired from the React UI to the Express API and persisted in SQLite.

evidence.note: Add flow posts to the API and updates state.
Delete endpoint backs the UI button.

items.improvementTip: Re-fetch or reconcile with the server response after toggling so UI and DB can't drift.
items.probeQuestion: Walk me through what happens, from click to database, when I tick a todo as done.

items.summary: Routes are RESTful and live in their own router; the DB is a separate module. PATCH returns {ok:true} instead of the updated todo, and there is no 404 for unknown ids.

evidence.note: Router mounted under a clear resource path.
No 404 when the id doesn't exist.

items.improvementTip: Return 404 when changes === 0, and return the updated row from PATCH.
items.probeQuestion: What status code should PATCH /api/todos/999 return if that todo doesn't exist?

items.summary: Component split is fine for the size, but fetch errors are never caught or shown.

evidence.quote: export default function TodoItem({ todo, onToggle, onDelete }) {

evidence.note: No .catch; a down API leaves a silent empty list.

items.improvementTip: Add an error state and show a message when a request fails.
items.probeQuestion: What does the user see if the server is down when the page loads?

items.improvementTip: Move the API URL to an env variable.
items.probeQuestion: Why did you hardcode the API URL?

items.summary: The client blocks empty titles, but the server inserts whatever it gets. A null title would hit the NOT NULL constraint and throw a 500.
items.improvementTip: Validate on the server too and return 400 with a message.
items.probeQuestion: If I call your POST endpoint with curl and no body, what happens?

items.summary: README has run steps, but a .env with a password is committed.

evidence.quote: Run the server: `cd server && npm install && node index.js`

items.improvementTip: Add .env to .gitignore and commit a .env.example instead.
items.probeQuestion: How would you keep secrets out of a public repo?

overallSummary: A small, working full-stack todo app with a clean Express + SQLite backend and a simple React UI. The main gaps are server-side validation and error handling, which are very normal at intern level.
topStrengths: Clear separation of routes and DB
growthAreas: Showing API errors in the UI
